clue.text: Viceroy's son provided with a carriage

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A viceroy's boy has been given his own carriage to ride about in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Viceroy's' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'provided with' simply links the son to the carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor ruling on behalf of the Persian king, so a regional ruler for a monarch.

clue.text: Maybe it's more a producer of spray

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be arranged otherwise, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some object is more of a spray device.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IT'S MORE A rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: A call soldiers are expected to rise to

definitions.text: A call soldiers are expected to rise to

parts.words: A call soldiers are expected to rise to
parts.note: a military bugle call that wakes troops in the morning, rising to it meaning getting out of bed

explanation.surface: A challenge that troops should rise to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise to' suggests meeting a challenge, but here it is literally getting up in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal sounded to wake soldiers at dawn.

clue.text: Old person using boarding-house with hesitation

parts.note: a pension is a continental boarding-house
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An elderly lodger hesitantly takes a room in a guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner is someone retired and drawing a pension, typically elderly.

clue.text: Like one of this man's chairs when occupied by a woman?

definitions.text: Like one of this man's chairs when occupied by a woman?

parts.words: Like one of this man's chairs when occupied by a woman?
parts.note: the furniture designer's name is read as a chair with a female sitter on it: SHE on top, in a playful split of the surname

explanation.surface: A question about how a designer's famous chairs look when a lady sits in one.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer whose name is attached to a style of chair; the clue plays on the surname starting with a woman's pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was the cabinet-maker whose elegant chairs gave his name to a furniture style.

clue.text: Moral reflections about 7 in More's sonnets, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the sin inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the words may be differently arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 7-down's answer is a transgression, so a sin

explanation.surface: Thoughts on moral wrongdoing found in Thomas More's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MORE'S SONNETS into SERMON STONES, and SIN goes in. The phrase is from As You Like It. The grid prints SEAMONS, an OCR slip for SERMONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's phrase means finding moral lessons in nature, as homilies drawn from stones.

clue.text: Regular practice of revellers in East

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a riotous crowd or party of revellers
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: The habit of party-goers out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rout' here is the old sense of a disorderly crowd or large party, not a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, habitual way of doing things.

clue.text: Lock out of resort for transgression of law

indicators.note: out of here means outside, so the lock goes around the resort

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Someone is shut out of a holiday resort for breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock out' suggests barring someone, but 'Lock' is a lock of hair, placed outside SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is an unlawful intrusion, an offence against the law.

clue.text: Absence of power when lacking a titled class

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: no ability is an absence of power

explanation.surface: A powerless state when there is no aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: NO ABILITY loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: The nobility is the aristocratic class whose members hold titles such as duke or earl.

clue.text: He calls meeting with the weird sisters about the new king

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the coven goes round the letter for new

parts.note: the Weird Sisters of Macbeth are three witches, and a group of witches is a coven
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword stand-in for a reigning monarch

explanation.surface: Someone summons a gathering with Macbeth's three witches to discuss the new monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints CONVENEA, an OCR slip for CONVENER: the wordplay plainly builds CONVENER, and the crossing 5-down is likewise misprinted with A for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A convener is the person who summons a committee or assembly to gather.

clue.text: Magnificent federation of states backed by bishop

indicators.note: backed means written backwards, so the federation's two letters are turned round

parts.note: US, the United States, is a federation of states
per is Latin for by, as in miles per hour
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A grand union of states gets support from a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns US into SU; 'by' is not a link but gives PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb and magnificent are synonyms, both meaning outstandingly fine or splendid.

clue.text: Incentive announced by speaker in old language

indicators.note: something a speaker announces is heard, not read, so a soundalike spelling is wanted

parts.note: a fillip is a stimulus or incentive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker announcement offers some motivation in an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in old language' looks like one phrase, but only 'language' is the definition; IN and O (old) are pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Filipino is the national tongue of the Philippines, based on Tagalog.

clue.text: Scatter, having lied disgracefully about the odds

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the odds
disgracefully suggests the word lied is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds on a horse at the start of a race

explanation.surface: Someone scatters a crowd after shamelessly lying about the betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgracefully' makes DIEL from LIED, and 'about' puts SP inside it after DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or disperse, as mist or a crowd is scattered.

clue.text: Said to make advances by love note, being friendless

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, so a soundalike spelling is used

parts.note: to make advances of money is to lend, so loans
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A suitor's romantic note, carrying his advances, leaves him alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make advances' suggests courtship, but here it is lending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonesome means solitary and lonely, as a person with no companions feels.

clue.text: Herculean figure that is carried by beast on island

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the beast's letters go around the abbreviation

parts.note: a mule is a beast of burden
SC, scilicet, is Latin for namely, that is
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A Hercules figure being carried on an animal's back across an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SC goes inside MULE, then MAN follows; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongman of great physical power is likened to the mythical hero Hercules.

clue.text: An actor once for the gallows?

definitions.meaning: Sir Herbert Beerbohm ... was a celebrated Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager
the gallows was traditionally called the ..., as in the hanging ...

explanation.surface: Asking whether a former actor ended up being hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Beerbohm Tree was the famous actor-manager, and the hanging tree is an old name for a gibbet.

clue.text: It's three times less at the end of the line

parts.note: ter is Latin for three times, used in prescriptions
minus means less

explanation.surface: Something three times smaller at the line's end.
explanation.walkthrough: TER, Latin for three times, may be unfamiliar; it appears in old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final station on a railway or bus route.

clue.text: Way to divide English prize? One way

indicators.note: dividing the phrase means going inside it, so the way sits within

parts.note: an award is a prize
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A method of splitting an English prize, one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: ST goes into E+AWARD after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastward names a direction of travel, so it is a single compass bearing.

clue.text: Catch sight of key agent

parts.note: E is a musical key
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Spotting the main secret operative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective meaning main, but it is the musical key E.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to glimpse or notice something at a distance.

clue.text: Concerning pound notes scattered around the floor

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the word for concerning
scattered means spread in disorder, so the letters of notes are rearranged

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: About banknotes strewn around on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' makes ENTSO from NOTES, and 'around' puts RE inside after ENT, before L.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a mezzanine, a low storey between the ground and first floors.

clue.text: Goin' to pieces, say, in this vessel?

indicators.note: say means spoken aloud, so a soundalike spelling is used

parts.note: going to pieces is panicking, the dropped g matching the clue's informal goin'

explanation.surface: Someone falling apart in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lacks its letter count in print. A pannikin is a small metal drinking cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannikin is a small metal cup or pan, a drinking container.

clue.text: Relative's £1,000 added to by Society

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
on means in addition, as in 'with tax on'

explanation.surface: A family member's thousand-pound gift is topped up by an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Relative's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is a family member, the son of one's son or daughter.

clue.text: Well-bred chap taking fish

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A refined man accepting fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means polite and refined, as someone well brought up would be.

clue.text: Revolt in vessel carrying metallic elements

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the vessel's letters go round the elements

parts.note: MY, motor yacht, is a ship prefix standing for a vessel
U is the chemical symbol for uranium, a metal
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: An uprising on board a ship laden with metal ores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. 'metallic elements' supplies two metals, U (uranium) and TIN, which sit inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is a rebellion, particularly by sailors against their officers.

clue.text: Forbearing towards books containing Lear's Nonsense

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the books and towards wrap the rearranged name

parts.note: to means towards
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse, and here nonsense says his name is jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Being patient about books that include Edward Lear's nonsense verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonsense' turns LEAR into LERA, which goes between TO and NT. Lear wrote famous nonsense poems such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerant and forbearing both describe someone patient and willing to put up with things.

clue.text: Some people on the phone are rather more forthcoming

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them

parts.words: people on the phone are rather

explanation.surface: Callers on the telephone tend to be rather chattier than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'phone are rather'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming nearer and being more forthcoming both mean approaching closer.

clue.text: Identify exotic liquor in a so-called one

parts.note: to name is to identify
sake is Japanese rice wine, a foreign drink

explanation.surface: Picking out a foreign spirit in something described as such.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply describes the foreign drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A namesake is a person or thing called by the same name as another.

clue.text: Painstaking but ill-used, poor soul

indicators.note: ill as in ill-treated tells us the word used is mistreated, so its letters are rearranged
poor suggests a wretched version of the word soul, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A careful worker, though mistreated, is a pitiable individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' turns USED into SEDU and 'poor' turns SOUL into LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedulous means diligent and persevering, showing great care in work.

clue.text: Hose is unconventional — only available in new style

indicators.note: available in means found inside, so the rearranged letters sit within the style abbreviation

parts.note: NS stands for New Style, the Gregorian calendar dating

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion note that these stockings are unusual and only come in a fresh design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' makes YLON from ONLY, which sits between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, and hose is the general word for stockings and tights.
